tiers.message: A product-led first-order nudge: best sellers and a sampler, no discount yet.
Brewing guides and new arrivals, with one first-order offer at the store's cap after 2 weeks.
Test subject lines that ask for a click (a short quiz, pick your tea); opens alone prove little.
A 2-email sunset asking whether they still want the emails; suppress non-clickers only after the owner says yes.
The welcome series, not campaigns, until it has run.
Leave in the main newsletter until they have received 3 emails.

plan.message: Early access to new harvests and limited lots, a handwritten thank-you in the next parcel, a review or referral ask.
plan.offer_rule: No discount. Perks only: early access and first pick of limited teas.

plan.message: A 3-email comeback over 3 weeks: a personal note from the owner, what's new in teas like the ones they bought, then the offer.
plan.offer_rule: The store's cap (15% off) in the last email only, with a minimum spend of $75, their own average order.
plan.frequency: 3 emails over 3 weeks, then 2 a month

plan.message: Refill reminders for the teas they reorder, and a step up to larger tins.
plan.offer_rule: No blanket discount. Free shipping on refills at most.

plan.message: The post-purchase flow (brewing guide, how to store tea), then a second-order email at day 33, a week before the store's median 40-day gap between first and second order.
plan.offer_rule: No discount in the first 30 days. A second-order offer only if the owner already runs one.

plan.message: Discovery: teas close to what they bought, brewing tips, a bundle that adds a new category.
plan.offer_rule: No discount. A bundle priced as the store already prices bundles.

plan.message: What's new since their last order, and a reorder link for what they bought before.
plan.offer_rule: At most half the store's cap (7% off), with a minimum spend of $35, their own average order.

plan.message: Why people come back: best sellers among repeat buyers, a sampler, reviews.
plan.offer_rule: One offer at the store's cap (15% off), once, with a minimum spend of $40.

plan.message: Content first (seasonal teas, brewing guides), one offer, then a sunset for anyone who still doesn't click.
plan.offer_rule: One email at the store's cap (15% off), with a minimum spend of $30, then the sunset. Suppressing anyone who still doesn't click waits for the owner's yes.

findings: Best customers are 31 people (12.4% of buyers) and bring 38.0% of net revenue. Protect them: no discounts, early access.

Big spenders gone quiet: 20 customers who spent $6,923.62 (22.2% of revenue) and haven't ordered in a median 406 days. 14.3% of those mailed clicked in 90 days (all customers: 27.1%), so pair the comeback emails with the ad-audience file.
51.2% of buyers have ordered once. Repeat buyers placed their second order a median 40 days after the first, so the second-order email goes at day 33.
48 of 151 subscribers who never bought (31.8%) received 3 or more emails in 90 days with no open or click. Run the 2-email sunset before anything else is sent to them.

klaviyo_segment_conditions.historic_clv: Not available: Klaviyo shows Historic CLV (predictive analytics) only from 500 buyers with orders, and this store has 250. Without it Klaviyo can't split on spend, so Best customers and Loyal are built as one segment, and Big spenders gone quiet and Dormant as one Gone quiet segment (R 1). The 13 Big spenders gone quiet with R 2 fall into Slipping or One-time buyers in Klaviyo. Use the static lists for the exact RFM members.
klaviyo_segment_conditions.how_to_build: Build in the order shown: Klaviyo doesn't apply rules in order, so each segment excludes the ones above it. Counts here are on the cleaned orders; Klaviyo counts every Placed Order (cancelled and refunded ones too), so live counts can run a little higher.
